title: Billing and Reimbursement for Acute PVD

posts.text: Hi Everyone, I received the email below form of my MIPS clients and not sure what to tell them. Can someone assist me with this? " Our understanding is that when a patient has a longstanding PVD in one eye (e.g., OD) and presents with an acute PVD in the fellow eye (OS), the diagnoses should be kept separate, with the acute designation applied only to the affected eye (e.g., PVD OD; PVD OS, acute). At the follow-up visit, the acute designation is removed, and the diagnosis is combined into a single bilateral PVD code. We have recently been informed that certain payers, particularly Humana and Molina, are issuing denials when bilateral conditions are split into unilateral diagnoses. This creates a challenge when splitting the diagnosis solely to meet the MIPS measure requirements. We would appreciate any guidance on how best to address this issue, or insight into how other practices are managing compliance with both MIPS and payer coding requirements in this instance." Thank you, Sherry

If we bill if we bill 90480 and 91321 (or 22) alone, the 90480 is paid.  This bundling issue just started in October.  Is anyone else experiencing this issue?
yes i am currently seeing the same issue as well

Are they seeing it as two admin codes bumping up against each other on the same date? Have you checked the provider news and provider resources, or Availity, clear claim connection, etc. for changes? You should always sign up for the provider newsletters and updates from the big plans to keep up with changes. There was probably a change announced for 10/1/25. I think I have seen where some plans (depending on Commercial, Medicaid/VFC) don't want 90480 if the pt. is under 19 y/o. They want 90460 with a modifier (if counseling was done and documented). Therefore, if you did the two, separate vaccines (with the face to face counseling) on the same date, and that was their policy, you would have to use two 90460 possibly. Either that or they might be looking for a 59 or XS to show it was two separate vaccines for 90480, 90460.

However, you have no contractual obligation with the insurer to do so, and you could bill the patient for that amount.

title: PRP, 0232T, performed in surgery to the same surgical site. Can we collect a non covered fee, for any reason, from an insured patient? Legality?

posts.text: I was asked to research if we can collect a "non covered" amount for PRP, 0232T, performed in surgery to the same surgical site. Says that 0232T performed in surgery to the same surgical site is inclusive to the surgical code. We can not collect from the patient or try to collect a non covered fee. At first I was told that the fee would be for the administration than I was told that it was for the technology. The rebuttal I received, when I told an office no, to collecting, was that AI, Chat GPT, says it could be done. I responded that the PRP could be given in the office, can be done, we can collect and have the patient sign a waiver/ABN. The other rebuttal received was that other physicians in the state, collect $ X from patients for PRP done in surgery. If the other offices don't get the non covered fee the surgery would be cancelled. My response is that the 2 rebuttals will not hold up in court. What is the legality of this? What if any, legal ramifications will there be if it is discovered that a "non covered" fee is collected for PRP done in surgery to the same surgical site.

This is an old thread with discussion about it. Ah, the age old PRP argument... I don't think anything has changed with this. The "kit" may be billable by the facility but the performance during the surgery is still inclusive as far as I know. title: 98926 with 50 modifier denial from Horizon NJ Health

posts.text: We billed 98926 with 50 modifier since the procedure was performed bilaterally however Horizon NJ Health denied stating "The procedure code is inconsistent with the modifier used or a required modifier is missing". so how do we bill this claim and get paid?

98926 is for 3-4 body regions involved. Body regions referred to by the CPT book are cervical region, thoracic region, lumbar region, sacral region, pelvic region, lower extremities, upper extremities, rib cage region, abdomen and viscera region. 98925 - 1-2 body regions involved 98927 - 5-6 body regions involved 98928 - 7-8 body regions involved 98929 - 9-10 body regions involved

bilateral modifiers are not applicable to osteopathic manipulative treatment codes. These services are reported based on the number of body regions treated rather than laterality, so the bilateral concept does not apply.

Dawson, I have personally contacted our Medicare medical director and have been speaking with him a good portion of the day and he states that a physician can not function as a locum for a NPP.
